thread:
pagerbot: INCIDENT: High GPU queue growth detected in us-east-1. Alerting on-call. severity=sev2

ashley_m: got the page, jumping in. seeing sustained queue rise on gpu-pool-a, 5m qps +120% 

jon_k: same graphs. autoscaler did a couple of scale ops but new nodes not joining; pods stuck in ContainerCreating. k8s events show mount timeouts.

kevin_chiu: mounting errors look like NFS timeout on /var/cache/prefix. that could explain prefix cache warm misses and reduced throughput.

anita_r: customers reporting 429s and 3-5s tail latency. staging shows continuous-batching window jumped from 50ms -> 400ms in the last config rollout. can we confirm config?

sam_runtime: i see a config change at 3098122900 from deploy-bot for continuous_batch_window=400ms and prefix_cache_ttl=30s. rolling restart started ~3098123000.

ml_infra: that aligns — recent PR adjusted batching heuristics to favor latency smoothing; likely increased batching causing backlog on GPUs. combined with prefix cache misses (NFS) reduces throughput dramatically.

sre_bot: @channel Pager on-call: ashley_m (primary). Please ack and coordinate handoff if needed.

ashley_m: ack. plan: 1) stop rollout / rollback batch config, 2) reduce new requests to problematic pool via routing rule, 3) warm prefix cache or fallback to hot cache, 4) if still saturated, spin up reserved pool (dedicated) and shift traffic.

jon_k: executing rollback now — reverting continuous_batch_window to 50ms in configmap db. applying patch: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env daemonset/runtime CONT_BATCH_WINDOW=50ms --record
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/runtime -n inference
```

kevin_chiu: while that rolls, i'm investigating NFS mount timeouts. hitting mount flapping on 3 nodes. remediating with node drain/unsched to let mounts reattach.

anita_r: routing change ready — adding a temporary route to send 30% of traffic from hostpool=us-east-1 to dedicated-reserve-2. command: 
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","weight":{"dedicated-reserve-2":30,"us-east-1":70}}
```

sam_runtime: route applied. also enabled a circuit-breaker on high-latency tokens to return fast 503 to avoid long tails.

ml_infra: observed prefix-cache missrate spike from 2% -> 48% after restart. warm fallback disabled by config bump. switching fallback on: 
```yaml
prefix_cache:
  fallback_on_miss: true
  warm_on_start: true
```

jon_k: rollback completed, daemonset pods restarted. early signs: batch latency dropping, queue growth plateauing.

ashley_m: nice, thanks. kevin, status on mounts?

kevin_chiu: reattached mounts to 2 nodes after drain/recreate. one node still in CrashLoopBackOff due to kubelet OOMkubelet - isolating it.

anita_r: customers: three high-usage tenants flagged. Customer A (payments-prod) had 30% error increase for 18m, Customer B (chat-saas) 429 spikes for 12m, Customer C (internal dev) 5m. we should prepare post-incident comms.

ashley_m: agree. i'll draft a short postmortem note. For now, mitigation checklist: rollback batching config ✅, route shift ✅, prefix cache fallback enabled ✅, NFS mounts stabilized partial ✅, reserved pool on standby.

ml_infra: metrics: token throughput recovering from 40k/t to ~85k/t in the last 6m. tail latency median back to 120ms, p99 down from 2.8s to 520ms.

sam_runtime: watch: still occasional bursts where autoscaler does not kick due to controller lock contention. i'm restarting autoscaler controller to clear the lock.

jon_k: restart done. autoscaler now sees free node capacity and is scheduling pods to dedicated-reserve-2 where routed.

ashley_m: OK live mitigation looks stable. moving to handoff to post-incident review. who's owning the RCA? I nominate kevin for storage (NFS), ml_infra for batching heuristics, sam_runtime for autoscaler lock.

kevin_chiu: taking storage RCA. initial hypothesis: mount client-side retries exposed by rolling restart + transient NFS broker load. will gather kernel logs, mountd traces.

ml_infra: taking batching RCA. hypothesis: config change to continuous_batch_window inadvertently disabled prefix cache warm/fallback and increased per-request aggregation causing larger per-gpu batch sizes and queueing. will run controlled A/B test with smaller window and warm_on_start enabled.

sam_runtime: taking autoscaler RCA. likely lock contention due to long list API calls during high-queue churn. will add better backoff and metrics.

anita_r: i'll own customer comms + SLO hit calc. initial SLO impact: payments-prod breached 99.9% latency for 18m; will compute token-level cost and impacted requests count.

ashley_m: great. final ops note: keep route in place for 60m, monitor for 30m without rollback reapplication. if queue growth resumes, escalate to bring forward reserved pool scale.

pagerbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigations applied, severity downgraded to sev3. Continue monitoring.

ashley_m: handing off to follow-up channel #incidents-postmortem. I'll post RCA owners + timeline. Thanks everyone. :team-heart:

sre_bot: This thread will be archived and linked to incident-3098123456 in the tracker.
